gaps.sentence: Such ___ the chaos at the airport that hundreds slept on the terminal floor.
gaps.explanation: 'Such was the chaos that…' — emphatic fronting of 'such' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ she won the marathon, but she also broke the course record.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only has she won' — inversion with the present perfect auxiliary.

gaps.sentence: Only when the audit was complete ___ the accounts released.
gaps.explanation: Only when X happened were the accounts released — inversion after only when.

gaps.sentence: Not until the second edition ___ the book become a bestseller.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until the second edition did the book become …'.

gaps.sentence: On no account ___ passengers open this door.
gaps.explanation: On no account should passengers… — formal prohibition.

gaps.sentence: Only after the third reminder ___ she reply to my email.
gaps.explanation: 'Only after' fronts the condition, so 'did she reply' inverts.

gaps.sentence: Only since the redesign ___ the app gained new users.
gaps.explanation: 'Only since the redesign has the app gained …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ anyone realise how close the firm was to insolvency.
gaps.explanation: "Little did anyone realise" = nobody realised — emphatic inversion with do-support.
